name: Luo Weidong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Aurora Mobile Ltd (Nasdaq: JG), Shenzhen
profile: Luo Weidong (Chris Luo) co-founded Shenzhen-based Aurora Mobile (JPush / Jiguang) in 2011 and has been chairman and CEO since May 2012. The mobile developer-services and big-data company, backed by IDG, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs, listed on Nasdaq in 2018; his stake (~30%) is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: PolyU says Aurora Mobile was the first company of its kind to list on Nasdaq (2018); Luo holds an MPhil in computing from PolyU and won its Outstanding Alumni Award for entrepreneurial achievement in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: During COVID-19, Luo led a research team behind a data platform that PolyU credits with supporting epidemic-containment work in 334 Chinese cities. Before Aurora he was GM of Shenzhen Zhiwo Information Technology (2007-2010).

public_contacts.value: Christensen Advisory - Xiaoyan Su, Xiaoyan.Su@christensencomms.com (IR agency named in Aurora Mobile press releases)

notes: Goes by Chris Luo. Some IR pages list ir@aurora-mobile.com instead of ir@jiguang.cn (company rebranding of IR domain). Named 2025 Greater Bay Area Strategic Emerging Industry Youth Leader (Feb 2026 release).

name: Xu Jie
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Phoenix Healthcare Group (now China Resources Medical, HKEX: 1515); current role not publicly reported
profile: Xu Jie (徐捷) founded Phoenix Healthcare, which grew from private hospitals into China's largest private hospital group by beds and visits and listed in Hong Kong in 2013 as the 'first private-hospital stock'. In 2016 China Resources took control; her family vehicle SpeedKey exited and she stepped down as chair. No public role since.
interesting_fact: Phoenix Healthcare's 2013 Hong Kong IPO made it the first listed private-hospital operator from mainland China; it pioneered investing in and managing public and SOE-owned hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2013 IPO prospectus, she bought the Jilin City Trauma Hospital (吉林市创伤医院) in 1988 and personally served as its legal representative and hospital director until 1995, before investing in hospitals in Dalian and Wuxi and founding Beijing Phoenix in 2007 with RMB45m of her own capital.
notes: Very low public profile since the 2016 China Resources takeover; company contacts (China Resources Medical) no longer represent her. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Raman Gupta
current_role: Promoter/long-time director of Metenere group (Metenere Limited, Metenere (Global) Ltd), Delhi; MD role at Metenere Limited reportedly ceased Oct 2024
profile: Raman Gupta is the Delhi-based promoter of Metenere, a non-ferrous metals group producing lead, lead alloys and oxides, aluminium products and tin. He has been a director of Metenere Limited since its 1997 incorporation; registry aggregators indicate a board change/amalgamation in Oct 2024. Hurun India listed him in 2017-2018.
interesting_fact: Metenere describes itself as one of India's biggest lead producers and the only producer of pure tin in India.
notes: Very little public coverage; sources are company-registry aggregators (Tofler, Qorpiq). Company website metenere.com appears to be parked/for sale. No published contact found; any outreach would need a verified company channel.

name: Shen Haiyin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zhiche Youxing Technology (智车优行, brand Singulato / 奇点汽车), Shanghai/Beijing; current status unclear
profile: Shen Haiyin (沈海寅) is an internet executive turned EV entrepreneur: a former VP at Kingsoft and Qihoo 360 and angel investor, he founded Zhiche Youxing in Oct 2014 to build smart EVs under the Singulato (奇点) brand, which raised at least seven rounds through 2020 and made him a Hurun unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: He decided to build cars after driving a Tesla in 2014: 'After experiencing a Tesla, I felt the auto industry was bound to change' (体验过特斯拉的车后，我就感觉汽车行业一定会变天).
deep_cut_fact: Not a total auto outsider: his first job after university was at Shanghai Delphi Automotive Air Conditioning, making car A/C components; in 2000 he moved to Japan and founded three companies there before ~15 years in China's internet industry.
notes: Singulato faced funding/wage-arrears problems and was reported heading toward bankruptcy around 2023 - avoid as a hook. No recent (2024-26) public activity found; no published contact.

name: Yan Xiaoping
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Eppen Group (伊品集团), a major shareholder of Guangdong Xinghu Technology (星湖科技, SSE: 600866)
profile: Yan Xiaoping (闫晓平) is co-controller, with husband Tie Xiaorong, of Eppen Group, whose Ningxia Eppen Biotech became one of China's top bio-fermentation makers of MSG, lysine and other amino acids. In 2022 Xinghu Technology acquired 99.22% of Eppen Biotech for shares and cash, making Eppen Group a large Xinghu shareholder.
interesting_fact: Eppen Biotech describes itself as ranking among the top three companies in China's bio-fermentation industry (MSG, lysine, threonine and other amino acids, largely for food and animal feed).
notes: Very private; appears only in shareholding disclosures (e.g. 2024 equity-change report showing she and Tie Xiaorong each hold 28.30% of Eppen Group). Best institutional route would be Xinghu Technology's board office via its exchange filings; no personal/office contact published.

name: Peter Lammer
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO/CTO of Sophos (Oxford cybersecurity company, taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2020); no current executive role found
profile: Dr Peter Lammer co-founded Sophos with Jan Hruska in Oxfordshire in 1985, initially making encryption software before pivoting to anti-virus; it grew into a major global security vendor. He served as co-CEO and later stayed on the board after Steve Munford became CEO. His stake, realised through later investment rounds, the 2015 LSE IPO and 2020 Thoma Bravo buyout, is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Sophos started in a semi-detached house in Kidlington, Oxford: 'just the two of them, a grand piano, and a German Shepherd dog.'
deep_cut_fact: Before security software, Lammer and Hruska's first venture was the AC-86, a portable computer designed to run DOS 1; only one prototype was ever built. A Norwegian distributor's suggestion later steered them from DES/RSA encryption tools into anti-virus.
notes: Holds an Oxford doctorate and Warwick undergraduate degree (per MarketScreener). Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Sophos press office no longer represents him.

name: Li Lianzhu
current_role: Chairman, Guangzhou Shangpin Home Collection (尚品宅配, SZSE: 300616); member of the National Committee of the CPPCC
profile: Li Lianzhu (李连柱) moved from software into furniture: after co-founding design-software maker Yuanfang Software, he founded Shangpin Home Collection in 2004, pioneering made-to-measure whole-home furniture with a C2B+O2O model. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017. At the 2026 Two Sessions he pushed AI and 3D printing for personalised manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Shangpin was the first home-furnishing company to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board (2017); in 2026 Li argued AI plus 3D printing can deliver truly 'one person, one product' (一人一品) customised furniture.
deep_cut_fact: Before furniture, Li co-founded Guangzhou Yuanfang Software (圆方软件) in 1994 with university classmates, building interior-design and furniture design software - the IT roots behind Shangpin's digital custom-furniture model.
notes: Active public figure (CPPCC member, gives media interviews at Two Sessions). Company IR is handled by board secretary He Yubing; best formal route is Shangpin's investor-relations channel / SZSE Hudongyi platform. No published email verified in sources checked.

name: Aruna Wadhawan
current_role: Former promoter-shareholder of Dewan Housing Finance Corporation (DHFL), Mumbai; no current public role confirmed
profile: Aruna Wadhawan is a member of the Wadhawan promoter family of DHFL, the Mumbai housing-finance company; NSE records list her among DHFL's promoters from 2006 to 2019. DHFL collapsed in 2019 and was acquired by Piramal through insolvency in 2021, so the shareholding behind her 2018 Hurun listing no longer exists.
notes: Not a suitable podcast guest: DHFL's former promoters are subject to major fraud investigations and SEBI/CBI actions (mainly against Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan); her own role appears passive. No public profile or published contact. Registry aggregators show her DIN as deactivated.

name: Yan Hua
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Farben Information Technology (法本信息, SZSE: 300925); controlling shareholder (~28%)
profile: Yan Hua (严华, b. 1977) controls and runs Farben Information Technology, a Shenzhen software outsourcing and digital-transformation services firm founded in 2006 that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in December 2020. He also chairs the affiliated Shenzhen Farben Electronics and Shanghai Farben Electronic Technology.
interesting_fact: Farben provides software R&D, testing and digital-transformation engineering services, largely as an outsourced development partner to large tech and financial clients; Yan holds about 105.5 million shares (28.13%).
deep_cut_fact: Before building Farben, Yan started out in sales - he was sales director at Shenzhen Kairong Industrial (深圳市凯荣实业) - and later completed a doctorate while running the company.
notes: Low media profile. Board secretary is Wu Chao (吴超); IR channel via SZSE filings/Hudongyi is the formal route. No published email found on the company site.

name: Wang Zhidong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Beijing Dianji Technology (点击科技, maker of Lava-Lava IM/collaboration software); also founded ed-tech venture Xiaonei-wai (校内外, 2013)
profile: Wang Zhidong (王志东), a Peking University graduate and pioneering software engineer, built Chinese-language Windows platforms, founded Stone Rich Sight (SRS) and in 1998 merged it with Sinanet to create Sina, serving as its CEO until 2001. He then founded Dianji Technology (Dec 2001), backed by Fidelity and later Lenovo, focused on IM and web collaboration, and later moved into online education.
interesting_fact: As Sina's founding CEO he took one of China's first big internet portals to a Nasdaq IPO in 2000, making him one of the best-known faces of China's first dot-com generation.
deep_cut_fact: Before the internet, he was a star Windows programmer: he wrote the Chinese-language Windows platforms BDWin, Chinese Star (中文之星) and RichWin, starting in 1989 at a Zhongguancun computer firm with fewer than ten employees.
notes: No recent (2024-26) coverage of Dianji found; current activity unclear. His 2001 departure from Sina was a board dismissal - avoid as a hook. No published contact found.

name: Weng Yaogen
current_role: Senior adviser (2025-2028) and co-controlling shareholder, Wuxi Huadong Heavy Machinery (华东重机, SZSE: 002685); executive director/GM of Wuxi Huadong Heavy Machinery Technology Group
profile: Weng Yaogen (翁耀根, b. 1958), a senior economist from Wuxi, built Huadong Heavy Machinery, a maker of port container cranes and heavy handling equipment, from a local machinery works. He chaired the listed company from Oct 2010 to May 2023 and in April 2025 was appointed its senior adviser; with concert parties he holds about 12% of the company.
interesting_fact: Huadong Heavy Machinery listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2012 and is known for container gantry and quayside cranes used in ports.
deep_cut_fact: His career began running township factories: he was director of the Wuxi Huazhuang Metal Machinery Factory (无锡华庄金属机械厂), then Wuxi Huazhuang Heavy Machinery Factory and Wuxi Huadong Heavy Machinery Factory, before incorporating the business in 2004.
notes: Low public profile; appears mainly in exchange filings. Formal route is Huadong Heavy Machinery's board office via SZSE disclosures. No published personal/office contact.

name: Xie Jianqiang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, Zhejiang Yotrio Group (浙江永强, SZSE: 002489), Linhai, Zhejiang
profile: Xie Jianqiang (谢建强, b. 1975) is one of the four co-controlling Xie family shareholders of Yotrio Group, a Linhai-based maker of outdoor leisure furniture, sun umbrellas and tents sold largely to Western retailers. He has been vice chairman and president since July 2019 and holds about 97.6 million shares directly.
interesting_fact: Yotrio is one of China's largest outdoor-furniture exporters, with more than 10,000 employees making patio furniture, parasols and tents.
deep_cut_fact: He started in the business as deputy GM of Taizhou Yongqiang Crafts (台州永强工艺品), the handicrafts company from which Yotrio grew, before rising to vice chairman and president.
notes: Low media profile. Company board secretary is Wang Hongyang; formal route via Yotrio's board office/SZSE disclosures. Research for this record was limited (web search budget exhausted mid-lane).

name: Lai Chunlin
current_role: Chairwoman and General Manager, Hubei Century Network Technology (盛天网络, SZSE: 300494), Wuhan; vice chair, Hubei Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Lai Chunlin (赖春临, b. 1977, Hubei) entered internet-cafe software in 2000 and in 2006 co-founded Shengtian (Century) Network, launching the 'Yiyou' (易游) internet-cafe management platform. She took it public on ChiNext in Dec 2015 - Hubei's first listed internet company - and has since expanded into game publishing and IP operations (Tianxi Huyu acquisitions 2019/2021). She owns ~24%.
interesting_fact: Shengtian was the first internet company from Hubei province to list (ChiNext, 2015); Lai was named one of the 'Optics Valley 30 innovators in 30 years'.
deep_cut_fact: Her company's roots are in China's internet cafes: in 2006 she launched 'Yiyou' (易游), a management platform for internet cafes; in 2023 she proposed esports hotels as offline entry points to the metaverse at a Wuhan developer summit.
notes: Hurun's 'Shanda' refers to Shengtian Network (盛天网络), not Chen Tianqiao's Shanda. Active in Hubei business associations; donated RMB1m to Hubei Red Cross in 2020. Formal route via company board office.
